title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-breadcrumbs-8
content:
Context:
- User-reported latency spikes and increased cold-start tail latency on dedicated GPU pool for model-family `redwood-13b-opt` during growth hours (US-east peak). Suspect autoscale warmup / scheduling thrash.
- Incident started ~2026-02-24 21:10 UTC; noisy neighbor? scheduling controller flapping nodes through the night.

What I've tried so far (commands + snippets):
1) Check pool and node state
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool-13b --selector=pool=dedicated-13b -o wide\  <-- shows pods in CrashLoopBackOff and Pending intermittently

2) Describe recent scheduling events for a sample pod:
- kubectl describe pod redwood-13b-serve-72k4 -n dedicated-pool-13b\  Events show repeated FailedScheduling: "Insufficient resources: cpu, nvidia.com/gpu" followed by SuccessfulScheduling after a few minutes.

3) Check autoscaler controller logs (controller-agg) around incident window:
- kubectl logs controller-manager-0 -n infra --since=3h | egrep "autoscale|scale|warmup|provision"
  Output (truncated):
  2026-02-24T20:59:07Z INFO autoscaler: scaling up pool dedicated-13b desired=6->9 reason=queue_backlog
  2026-02-24T21:02:12Z WARN autoscaler: provision_timeout for batch-reqs, marking nodes as degraded
  2026-02-24T21:06:48Z INFO scheduler: allocating instance g4dn.xlarge (warmup=false) to pool dedicated-13b
  2026-02-24T21:08:00Z INFO autoscaler: successful warmup detected for 2 nodes
  2026-02-24T21:10:15Z INFO autoscaler: scaling down pool dedicated-13b desired=9->5 reason=low_utilization
  2026-02-24T21:12:03Z ERROR autoscaler: attempt to remove node node-az1-7 failed: active pods > 0

4) Node warmup probe logs (from infra metrics):
- warmup_probe_counter{node="node-az1-7"} 0
- model_kv_cache_loaded{node="node-az1-7", model="redwood-13b-opt"} 0
  -> suggests model weights not fully warmed/cached before traffic routed.

5) Recent scheduling policy changes: rolling config applied 2026-02-23 02:00 UTC to reduce warmup threshold from 120s -> 30s (PR: github.com/.../pr/813). Might be too aggressive.

Errors / snippets captured in logs:
- "Failed to attach GPU: device busy" (kubelet)
- "eviction: node under memory pressure" repeated during scale events
- "model load timeout after 45s" from serving-runtime (expected threshold previously 120s)

Hypotheses:
- H1: Warmup threshold reduction (120s->30s) causes autoscaler to mark nodes ready sooner and then scale-down prematurely because probes show no active KV cache, leading to repeated cold starts and increased tail latency.
- H2: Provision timeout path marking nodes as degraded prevents proper reuse, causing thrash between scale-up and scale-down.
- H3: Placement constraints (anti-affinity) + AZ imbalance cause scheduling delays and GPU attachment failures under churn.
- H4: Workload burstiness interacts with autoscaler cooldowns -> autoscaler oscillates (see desired=6->9->5 sequence).

Immediate next steps (to validate / mitigate):
- Roll back warmup threshold change in a canary: set warmup threshold back to 120s for a single pool and observe. (PR rollback prepared: github.com/.../pr/820)
- Disable aggressive scale-down (increase scale-down cooldown from 60s -> 300s) for dedicated-13b pool to reduce thrash.
- Add temporary leash: prevent autoscaler from touching nodes flagged as "degraded" for 10m.
- Force probe run: trigger model prewarm job for 3 nodes in pool dedicated-13b (kubectl exec prewarm-job) and observe model_kv_cache_loaded metrics.

Questions to ask / followups:
- @Priya: can infra increase node boot logging duration to capture attachment failures?
- @Samir: do we have historical node warmup metrics for last 30 days to compare success rates?
- Should we add a server-side circuit-breaker to avoid routing traffic to nodes without KV cache?

Notes on mitigation timeline:
- T+0 (now): increase scale-down cooldown and queue a prewarm job for 3 nodes (safe, low-risk).
- T+30m: monitor tail latency p95/p99 and node churn rate.
- T+2h: if improvement, roll warmup threshold rollback to staging and run A/B.

Observations from user reports:
- Several customers in account CS-209 reported 10-30% higher median latency for a short window each night.
- Cost increase due to repeated node warmups (more provisioning events).

Raw commands used (copyable):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool-13b --selector=pool=dedicated-13b -o wide
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n dedicated-pool-13b
- kubectl logs controller-manager-0 -n infra --since=4h | egrep "autoscale|scale|warmup|provision"
- kubectl exec -n infra deploy/prewarm-job -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -sS http://localhost:8080/prewarm?model=redwood-13b-opt'

Potential follow-ups to convert into runbook items:
- Define safe warmup threshold defaults per model size/class (e.g., 30s for 7B, 120s for 13B+).
- Autoscaler heuristic: only allow scale-down if model_kv_cache_loaded metric > 0 for N nodes OR node uptime > X minutes.
- Add circuit-breaker to route only to nodes that report KV cache ready or have served at least one request.

Sticky notes / TODOs (for me):
- [ ] Run prewarm on 3 nodes and capture model_kv_cache_loaded after 10/30/60s.
- [ ] Apply temporary cooldown tweak and monitor for 1h.
- [ ] Collate metrics for last 30 days for warmup success rate and churn frequency.
- [ ] Draft quick incident summary for morning ops channel (include customer impacts).

References / links:
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-4721
- PR that changed warmup threshold: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/813
- Rollback PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/820
- Slack thread: slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1677223345678

Last run of probes (metrics snapshot):
- time=2026-02-24T21:15:00Z p95_latency_pool_dedicated-13b=312ms p99=1.2s node_churn=6 events/10m

End notes: this is a working scratchpad. Will update after prewarm results and after we apply the cooldown tweak.
